subject: teams/{teamId} is world-readable while carrying raw Firebase UIDs in members[]
description: Surfaced by Mallory and confirmed as the real defect by Chris during the 420 review, 2026-09-26. Deliberately NOT folded into that fix. firestore.rules makes teams/{teamId} 'allow read: if true' so the podium and lobby work pre-auth, and members[] on that document carries raw Firebase UIDs - proven readable by an unauthenticated REST GET with no bearer token. memberNames[] is index-aligned with it, so a reader of the raw document has uid-to-name pairing for every student. CONSEQUENCE FOR AN EARLIER CLAIM OF MINE: I described replacing the uid/email display fallback with a Player-xxxx placeholder as a privacy fix. Half of that was overstated and the commit now says so. What it genuinely closed is the EMAIL fallback (real PII appearing nowhere else on the doc) and a uid being RENDERED as a person's name; it buys nothing against someone reading the raw document, because members[] is right there. Salting the placeholder with tournamentId closed cross-event correlation, which is real but narrower. THE ACTUAL FIX is architectural and needs its own four-way vote per Chris: the podium needs a public projection carrying no identifiers, and membership management moves off the public document or behind a Cloud-Function-mediated read. This is pre-existing (BUG-024's 'teams are public, Cloud Functions manage the parallel arrays' model), not introduced by recent work, but it should not quietly become permanent.
